issues.description: One patch doing three unrelated things — README reformat, example behavior change, and new tests
issues.detail: The PR title says 'add POST request tests' but the diff also rewrites README.rst formatting wholesale and changes things_advanced.py from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). Those are three separate patches. When this regresses in a year, bisect lands on a commit that touches everything. Split it: tests-only, example fix with its rationale, README cleanup as a separate mechanical change. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: README signature change `handle(ex, req, resp, params)` -> `handle(req, resp, ex, params)` is a silent behavior change buried in 'formatting'
issues.detail: Falcon's error handler signature is API-load-bearing. Flipping argument order in a README example, in a diff sold as test additions, is exactly the kind of thing that breaks downstream copy-paste users. Either this is correct and deserves its own commit with rationale, or it's wrong and must revert. It cannot ride along.

issues.description: The example change from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is unexplained and unmotivated
issues.detail: The PR description says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the actual diff switches to bounded_stream.read() with no argument. Those are not the same fix. Either justify why bounded_stream is the right call here (and put it in the commit message) or revert. Prose in a PR body is not a commit message.

issues.description: FAQ example has bad taste: dead branch and a redundant `or 0` after an already-checked None
issues.detail: `if req.content_length in (None, 0): 200 else: if req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`. The `or 0` is dead — we already excluded None and 0 in the outer branch. Reading 0 bytes would never happen here. This is the kind of special-case-noise that teaches readers the wrong pattern in a docs example. Simplify or delete.

issues.description: Test assertion uses `assert(result.status == ...)` — looks like a function call, isn't
issues.detail: `assert(x == y)` is a Python footgun: it parses as assert on a tuple-or-paren expression and behaves differently from `assert x == y` in edge cases (notably `assert(x, y)` which is always truthy). In a FAQ example that people will copy, write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`. Small thing, but docs examples set the house style.

issues.description: New tests have no docstrings, no comments, and rely on magic path '/1337/things' with no explanation
issues.detail: resp3/resp4 are fine as far as they go, but the maintainer six months from now reading these will wonder what user_id 1337 means and why Content-Length: '1' with empty body is the interesting case. One line of comment per test ('empty body but non-zero Content-Length should 400') costs nothing and pays for itself the first time someone debugs a failure.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. Submitted as 'add POST tests' but is actually three patches in a trench coat: new tests, an example behavior change (stream -> bounded_stream), and a sweeping README reformat that quietly flips an error handler argument order. The tests themselves are reasonable and the FAQ addition is a useful idea, but the FAQ example carries dead-branch logic and an `assert(...)` footgun that will be copy-pasted. Split this into separate commits, justify the bounded_stream switch in its own commit message, and either land the README signature change as its own deliberate patch or revert it. Then resubmit.
